core_obligations: Recall that the closed subset cut out by an intersection of ideals is the union of the closed subsets cut out by the individual ideals (the author's hint, proof line 4633).

For each choice of one root per variable, the evaluation map Phi_k kills J by construction, so its kernel J_k describes the points of Spec(R) that come from that choice of roots (proof lines 4631-4633).

Use primality to pass from a prime containing the intersection to a prime containing one J_k, and conclude that the image of Spec(S) to Spec(R) is exactly the closed subset defined by the intersection (proof lines 4631-4633).

difficulty_reason: The lemma describes the image of the spectrum map for a quotient S of a polynomial ring whose ideal contains, for each variable, a polynomial that is a product of linear factors with coefficients in the base ring (statement lines 4613-4628). For every choice of one root per variable one gets an evaluation map of R[T_1, ..., T_n] to R, hence an ideal J of the choice, and the assertion is that the image of Spec(S) to Spec(R) is exactly the closed subset defined by the intersection of all these ideals. The author's proof is one line plus a hint (proof lines 4631-4633): the hint is that the vanishing set of an intersection of ideals is the union of the individual vanishing sets. A reader has to combine that with the fact that a prime containing the intersection of finitely many ideals contains one of them, and with the identification of the fibre of the spectrum map over a prime with the evaluations that land in that prime. The lemma is used later in the section precisely to test set-theoretic properties of the map, so the identification is the content.
